ctor.rationale: `base(3, CardType.Attack, CardRarity.Rare, TargetType.AnyEnemy)` (Mangle.cs:27-30) == cost 3 / ATTACK / RARE / ANY_ENEMY.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new DamageVar(15m, ValueProp.Move)` + `new DynamicVar("StrengthLoss", 10m)` (Mangle.cs:19-23) == both numbers, both declared. The sim stores the loss POSITIVE and hands it to ManglePower, matching C#, which also passes the positive BaseValue and lets the power carry the IsPositive=false sign -- so the sign-aware power-typing bug class does not bite at the card level. Same shape as card/dark_shackles.

OnPlay.issue: C# applies the power unconditionally and the only gate is `Creature.CanReceivePowers` (Creature.cs:308-321), whose doc comment states that DEAD creatures can still receive powers -- it refuses only for a REMOVED corpse. The two agree for an ordinary kill (`CreatureCmd.Damage` runs `Kill` before returning, CreatureCmd.cs:409, and removal happens at 523-525) and diverge for a corpse whose removal was VETOED (`ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath`, CreatureCmd.cs:508; the sim's `retained_after_death`, cmds.py:100-104), because `is_gone` is `is_dead or escaped` (creatures.py:44-46). Observable through ViciousPower and any listener that fires on a power landing regardless of target liveness. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/bash's OnPlay entry (rule 3); LIVE. Damage 15 first, then ManglePower 10 -- amounts and order faithful (Mangle.cs:35-40). Presentation, folded in: the Ironclad heavy-anim helpers, WithHitFx, WithHitVfxSpawnedAtBase and the Strength hover tip.
